measurements.patch_alone_no_source_change: 0 conversions / 0 regressions across all 557 units and the 58-control gate - the compiler patch alone only narrows fun_002071c0's residual (91.111 -> 92.778%, isolated to that single unit, verified against every other unit's code_percent moving by < 0.001); the conversion to exact additionally required the paired source-shape fix below.

root_cause_diagnosis.method: Runtime instrumentation (fprintf traces at all 6 real INSN_ANNULLED_BRANCH_P assignment sites in reorg.c/mips.c on a rebuilt cc1, reading stderr while compiling just the failing function), not static source reading - three earlier static-reasoning theories about this mechanism were each disproven or found inert in this and a prior session; see docs/PROJECT_STATUS.md 'RESOLVED: the exact annul-branch mechanism, found by instrumentation not reading'.
root_cause_diagnosis.responsible_function: reorg.c fill_slots_from_thread (the else-if branch gated by #ifdef ANNUL_IFFALSE_SLOTS around line 2647), calling the real (non-stub) genattrtab-generated eligible_for_annul_false - confirmed present in genuine upstream FSF gcc-2.95.2 too via insn-attr.h's ANNUL_IFFALSE_SLOTS (not insn-config.h/genconfig.c, which several earlier sessions checked instead and found nothing).
root_cause_diagnosis.blind_spot: resource.c's mark_target_live_regs walks forward via next_insn_no_annul, which on encountering an already delay-filled branch (a SEQUENCE) returns just the branch sub-insn (XVECEXP(seq,0,0)) and never inspects the SEQUENCE's own delay-slot insn. So a register genuinely killed by the very next branch's delay slot can still show as 'needed' at that point, forcing reorg onto the annul-only path for an otherwise-plain-eligible delay-slot fill.
root_cause_diagnosis.reproduced_with: P1 baseline only, no other ASTRA patches applied - confirmed base GCC 2.9 behavior, not introduced by any prior patch in this stack.

fixture.paired_source_change: The promoted src/textbin/fun_002071c0.c also inverts the `ret1 != 0 return 1;` early-return guard into a `ret1 == 0 { ... } return 1;` nested-positive-guard shape (matching the project's established 'positive-guard/early-return inversion' pattern, e.g. fun_001ff288). This was a second, independent, unrelated residual (a branch-polarity/source-shape difference, not an annul defect) on the same function; both had to be fixed for the unit to reach 100%.

mechanism: config/mips/mips.c: new mips_r5900_unannul_redundant(), wired into MACHINE_DEPENDENT_REORG_AFTER_DBR_2 alongside mips_r5900_annul_dead_slots (P25). New default-on opt-out flag -mastra-unannul-redundant (mirrors P25's pattern: char* initialized to "" so it runs unless explicitly disabled).
role: Default: clear a branch's annulled (branch-likely) flag when reorg.c's generic delay-slot filler set it purely because its own liveness walk (mark_target_live_regs/next_insn_no_annul) treats the very next already-delay-filled branch as opaque and never looks at that branch's own delay-slot write. In the narrow case where that next branch's delay slot unconditionally overwrites the same register with a value independent of its old contents, and the next branch's own condition does not read that register, annulled and plain forms are behaviorally identical; retail keeps the plain form.
